review.why: Builds and publishes first-class n8n Agents through the agent tools: when to choose one over a workflow, the build sequence, approvals and debugging.
review.summary: Starts with a decision table (agent, workflow or AI Agent node), then five non-negotiables: send a memory block, never publish without approval, publish what the agent calls, gate risky tools, one change per call. It gives an eight-step build sequence, current limits, instruction-writing advice and an anti-pattern table. Twelve reference files hold the details.
strengths: Clear rule for choosing agent, workflow or AI Agent node
Publishing and channel connection always need the user's explicit yes
Anti-pattern table lists silent failures such as unpublished sub-agents
cautions: Needs an n8n instance with Agents enabled; some parts are marked temporary because the feature is changing
Twelve reference files are not read here
Test calls run real tools, so side effects can happen
